messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming/decode.p99 > 3.5s for the last 5m. Spike detected across us-west clusters. Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.internal/streams/decode
maria: seeing it too. us-west-1e nodes running kernel-build v2.14.0 with TRT 8.2.0 + FlashAttn v2.0.1. p99 jumped from ~800ms -> 4.2s. p95 up to ~1.1s. mostly on long contexts (>2048 tokens) and streaming endpoints.
kevin: logs show an uptick in page faults on affected hosts. example from gpu-17: "page_faults: 432, evictions: 29, r/o remap retries: 3". NVML shows increased memcopy stalls.
sre-ops: reproducing locally on staging with the same kernel build. Decode stalls around token 512-768, then resumes. suspect compilepath kernel change interacting with FlashAttn memory layout.
infra-jen: rollout history: kernel-build v2.14.0 rolled 02:12UTC via compile-pipeline #build-5123. Prior stable is v2.13.2. Change log includes a linker flag tweak: LTO_ENABLE=1 and a new allocator tweak: CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.8.
alex: can we confirm whether this is a kernel binary change or the TRT/FlashAttn binary change? Which artifact differs between 2.13.2 and 2.14.0?
maria: artifact diff shows new compile flag: -fno-wrapv removed, and FlashAttn was rebuilt with fused kernels enabled (FLASH_FUSE=1). TRT plugin also rebuilt with dynamic shared memory path.
kevin: small reproduction script attached in thread: ```python
# repro: stream 4k token prompt
for prompt in sample_prompts:
    resp = client.stream_generate(model="rwd-infer/gptx-1", prompt=prompt)
    measure_latency(resp)
``` results show gap: steady token throughput then 2-3s stall mid-stream.
sre-ops: paging traces (kernprof) show repeated kernel rebinds and allocator eviction when sequence length grows. Looks like combined effect of fused flash kernels + aggressive allocator = KV cache churn.
infra-jen: I'm pulling heaptrace and paging counters, will attach. Also checking disk swap pressure (should be 0) and cgroup memory limits.
customer-success: FYI several customers (account-ACME, account-Blueware) reported degraded streaming quality/perf. CS opened INC-9876.
oncall-temp: proposing immediate mitigations: 1) divert 25% traffic from affected us-west clusters to fallback pool (gptx-small-int8) 2) disable FLASH_FUSE flag in the runtime build and restart a canary subset 3) enable conservative KV-cache eviction (set eviction threshold to 0.95)
maria: I can prepare a quick image with FLASH_FUSE=0 and LTO_DISABLE=1 to test. Rolling to 2 hosts first.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary group gpu-17,gpu-18 -> image rwd-runtime:v2026-396-canary
kevin: while canary rolls, set routing rule: route 25% to dedicated-fallback via traffic-manager. I've created route change PR and applied.
sre-ops: metrics after canary spin-up: canary p99 back to ~900ms, p95 ~850ms. affected nodes still high. Looks promising.
maria: can confirm. Rolling canary to additional 8 hosts now. If stable after 10m, we'll proceed cluster-wide rollback.
ops-manager: also note impact on token cost due to retries/latency. Need an estimate for customer-impact email. CS, can you compile list of affected orgs and severity?
customer-success: compiling. initial list: ACME (high), Blueware (medium), two trial customers (low). Preparing template update.
infra-jen: patch note: the allocator change came from attempt to reduce tail OOMs; it inadvertently reduced buffer headroom. Reverting allocator patch alongside disabling fuse.
kevin: before full rollback, let's confirm no other regression: run synthetic long-context workloads and monitor page_faults, evictions, nvlink usage.
maria: synthetic tests running: long-context 8k tokens. Without FLASH_FUSE stalls disappear on canary build. Memory headroom stable.
alex: plan = rollback runtime build on all us-west nodes to rwd-runtime:v2026-395 (last stable), disable FLASH_FUSE in next build, and revert allocator patch. Rollout steps and rollback window?
oncall-temp: recommended rollout: 1) pre-check 5m health, 2) drain connections off each host gradually, 3) deploy, 4) monitor p95/p99 for 15m, 5) proceed. Rollout estimated 30-40m for whole region.
maria: starting region rollback now. Updating runbook with commands.
maria: RUNBOOK snippet:
```
# rollback runtime
for host in $(list-affected-hosts); do
  ssh $host sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime
  ssh $host sudo docker pull rwd-runtime:v2026-395
  ssh $host sudo docker tag rwd-runtime:v2026-395 rwd-runtime:current
  ssh $host sudo systemctl start redwood-runtime
  wait_for_health $host
done
# post-checks: curl /health, check page_faults, p99 metrics
```
kevin: scheduling 10m quiet window with customer-success for sensitive orgs. CS will send notice after 2nd host verified.
customer-success: sent initial advisory to ACME (we flagged as degraded performance, mitigation in progress). Getting logs from them for chronology.
sre-ops: halfway through rollback. So far 5/20 hosts rolled. p99 in region trending down: 4.2s -> 1.2s.
infra-jen: attaching kernel oops logs for one host where page_faults spiked: "kernel: compilepath: evict triggered at 0x7ff... allocator reclaim succeeded". Not showing OOM.
oncall-temp: decision: proceed full rollback. After rollback, create postmortem and schedule follow-up with runtime team to change default to FLASH_FUSE=0 until we verify memory model.
maria: full region rollback complete. Running extended 30m soak. Current p99 ~820ms, p95 ~700ms. Streaming stalls no longer reproducible on canary tests.
kevin: closing incident while we monitor. Create INC ticket summary: root cause = combined kernel allocator threshold change + FlashAttn fused kernels rebuild causing allocator churn and paging on long-context streams. Mitigation = rollback runtime to v2026-395, disable FLASH_FUSE, revert allocator threshold. Next steps = revert merge in compile pipeline, add regression test for long-context streaming, and add canary gating for FLASH_FUSE.
ops-manager: assign action items and timeline.
maria: action items: (1) runtime team: revert allocator patch and push new build without FLASH_FUSE (ETA 24h) (2) infra: add page_fault and eviction alert thresholds to SLO dashboard (ETA 48h) (3) eng-sre: add long-context synthetic test to pre-prod (ETA 72h)
alex: I'm taking handoff for overnight monitoring. @oncall-temp handing to @alex. Logging the handoff in pagerduty.
oncall-temp: handing off to alex. Details in #INC-9876. All relevant diffs in PRs: build-5123 (allocator), flashattn-rebuild-231.
alex: ack. I'll watch p99 and paging metrics and will page if re-escalation needed. Re-open thread for postmortem writeup.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: streaming/decode.p99 back below SLO for 20m. Marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:
